summary: Gulf states condemn Iran's attack on Bahrain, Russia hits Odesa's grid before a Trump-Xi-Putin meeting, Israel's coalition talks stall, and COP31 enters its last week.

question.text: Canada, Southeast Asian countries and others are trying to rely less on the US by trading more with China, and vice versa. If a country shifts its dependence from one big partner to another, what new risks might that create, and how would you judge whether the trade was worth it?

read.title: Strait of Hormuz explained: Why the Iran war threatens global energy flows
read.summary: A clear explainer on what a shipping chokepoint is, how much oil passes through Hormuz, and how mines and drones can disrupt it. Written in March, so check today's figures against the news.

topics.heading: Gulf states condemn Iran's drone attack on Bahrain as a third US carrier arrives
topics.summary: Gulf states condemned Sunday's Iranian drone attack on Bahrain, which Bahrain says it fully stopped, while the IRGC claims hits and more ships sunk near Hormuz.[^1][^2] A third US aircraft carrier entered the region, and the UN nuclear watchdog says it cannot track Iran's enriched uranium.[^2][^4]

lead.title: Iran attacks Bahrain in 'blatant challenge' to peace push

alsoReported.title: Iran says it targets US radar in Bahrain. What do we know?
Iran escalates threats against US forces and Gulf states as third American carrier arrives

article: Before dawn on Sunday, Bahrain issued its first nationwide alert in months, telling residents to move to a "safe location".[^1] Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) say six drones struck a US air-defence radar at Riffa Air Base; Bahrain says the drones were destroyed before reaching their targets, and the US had not commented on Sunday's claim.[^1][^3] It was the IRGC's second radar claim in three days. For the first, on Friday, US Central Command said it shot down two drones and nothing was damaged.[^3]

Neighbours reacted sharply. The head of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC, the six-country Gulf bloc) called the attack a "blatant challenge" to peace efforts, the UAE called it a "flagrant violation", and Qatar, which is carrying messages between Tehran and Washington, called it a "dangerous escalation".[^1] Gulf stock markets fell, with Qatar's index down 1.8%.[^1]

At sea, claims are growing but unconfirmed. The IRGC now says six vessels caught fire and sank in the strait since Sunday; none of this has been independently verified.[^2] Separately, the UK's maritime security agency (UKMTO) reported that a ship leaving the strait on Monday morning was hit by an unknown projectile, causing a fire but no casualties.[^2] The USS Theodore Roosevelt entered the US Central Command area on Sunday, joining two other carriers in what is expected to be a temporary build-up.[^2]

The nuclear question is getting harder to answer. A restricted report from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), seen by Bloomberg, says inspectors cannot verify where about 972 pounds of highly enriched uranium are, and IAEA chief Rafael Grossi says the agency cannot conclude that none has been diverted.[^4] Iran has ruled out regular monitoring "under the present circumstances", and the IAEA board meets in Vienna next.[^4]

Diplomacy continues alongside the fighting: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is due in Oman's capital, Muscat, on Tuesday, and Iran says it is still waiting for a US reply to seven conditions sent through Qatar.[^1][^3] My read: each side is testing the other's limits, and the week's mix of carrier moves, unverified sinkings and talks makes a misreading more likely than usual.
topics.differences: The IRGC says its drones hit a US radar; Bahrain says all were destroyed and US Central Command denied any damage from Friday's attack.[^1][^3] The IRGC's count of sunk or burning ships has risen from two to six; no independent source has confirmed any of them.[^2][^3]

topics.heading: Russia hits Odesa's power grid as the Kremlin confirms a Trump-Xi-Putin meeting
topics.summary: A large Russian drone attack left about 41,000 households in Odesa Oblast briefly without power, while Ukraine says it hit an airfield and refineries deep in Russia.[^5] Moscow confirmed Putin will meet Trump and Xi in Shenzhen on Nov 19.[^7]

lead.title: Ukraine war latest: Russia launches mass attack on Odesa Oblast as Ukraine strikes airfield, drone launch site in Russia

alsoReported.title: Russia, Ukraine Trade Air Attacks As US-Mediated Talks Fail To Break Diplomatic Deadlock
Moscow confirms Trump, Xi, Putin meeting in China

article: Overnight into Nov 15, Russia launched 132 long-range drones at Ukraine, of which Ukraine's air force says 106 were stopped.[^5] In Odesa Oblast, on the Black Sea, about 41,000 families temporarily lost power and six people were injured; across the country at least four people were killed and 69 injured over the day, according to Ukrainian officials.[^5] President Zelenskyy says Russia used more than 2,300 attack drones and 1,590 glide bombs in the past week.[^5]

Ukraine struck back at long range. Its General Staff says it hit the Akhtubinsk airfield, a drone base in Oryol and the Nizhnekamsk petrochemical complex and refinery, more than 800 km from the front, where local authorities confirmed damage and three injuries.[^5][^6] Russia's Defence Ministry says it shot down 533 Ukrainian drones overnight, a figure RFE/RL could not verify.[^6] Zelenskyy also blamed limits on SpaceX's Starshield service, saying interceptor drones lose contact above 161 km/h.[^6]

The diplomacy is moving to Asia. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that Putin, Trump and Xi Jinping will meet in Shenzhen on Nov 19, during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit; it would be the first meeting of the three.[^7] A senior US official says Trump will focus on Iran and nuclear weapons, not Ukraine, and expects no agreements.[^7] Arms control is a live issue because New START, the last US-Russia nuclear treaty, expired in February.[^7]

Talks on Ukraine itself are stuck. The Abu Dhabi round on Nov 10-11 brought no breakthrough, and US envoys then met Putin in Moscow.[^6] On the reported idea of trading Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskyy says Ukrainians would have the final say and that he would need guarantees like NATO's Article 5 "as an absolute minimum".[^5]

My read: with winter coming, both sides are aiming at energy targets to raise the cost of the war for the other, while the big-power meeting in Shenzhen may shape the talks without Ukraine in the room.
topics.differences: US officials say Ukraine is not on the Shenzhen agenda.[^7] Ukraine and Russia each report the other's losses in ways that cannot be checked: Russia's claim of 533 downed drones is unverified.[^6]

topics.heading: Israel's coalition talks stall ahead of a Knesset speaker vote; Hamas commander killed
topics.summary: Unity talks between Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud made no progress on Sunday, with a vote for Knesset speaker set for Tuesday.[^8] In Gaza, Israel killed Hamas's Rafah commander in an overnight strike.[^10][^11]

lead.title: No progress reported in Yashar-Likud unity talks; Netanyahu said open to excluding Ben Gvir

alsoReported.title: Senior Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza
Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas commander in Gaza

article: Israel is still without a new government after its election. Gadi Eisenkot, a former army chief whose Yashar party leads the anti-Netanyahu bloc, has the first chance to form a coalition. On Sunday his team and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud met for about an hour; their joint statement described a "businesslike atmosphere", but neither side will give up the prime minister's job.[^8]

The arithmetic is tight. In the 120-seat Knesset (parliament), Jewish-led parties opposed to Netanyahu hold 48 seats, Netanyahu's bloc 53, and Arab parties 19.[^9] A majority is 61. Eisenkot's camp is courting the ultra-Orthodox parties UTJ (7 seats) and Shas (6); Shas leader Aryeh Deri says his party is "going with Netanyahu".[^8][^9] Israel Hayom reports that Likud may drop far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir's party from a unity deal, though Netanyahu publicly insists on keeping all his allies.[^8] The first test comes Tuesday, when the Knesset votes on replacing its speaker; Yashar refused Likud's request not to nominate Matan Kahana.[^8]

In Gaza, the Israeli military says it killed Samir Abu Younis, 53, the commander of Hamas's Rafah brigade, overnight into Nov 15; Hamas's armed wing confirmed his death.[^10] Israel says he helped plan the Oct 7, 2023 attack.[^10] Al Jazeera reports the strike hit a tent sheltering displaced people in al-Mawasi and wounded two others.[^11]

Gaza's health ministry says at least 1,643 people have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire began, and reports 11 cold-related deaths as winter sets in.[^11] The truce has stopped the full war but not the killing, and it has not achieved Hamas's disarmament.[^10] My read: decisions on Gaza's next phase are likely to wait until Israel knows who will govern it.
topics.differences: Reuters reports Abu Younis was targeted "on a street"; Al Jazeera says the strike hit a tent of displaced people.[^10][^11] A UTJ source told Israeli TV there was progress with Eisenkot; UTJ's chair called that "entirely baseless".[^8]

topics.heading: COP31 enters its final week in Antalya with no agreed plan on fossil fuels or finance
topics.summary: The UN climate summit in Turkey starts its last week with ministers arriving and limited progress: countries still disagree on the main deal, adaptation money and fossil fuels.[^12][^13]

lead.title: COP31 Bulletin Day 6: Climate marchers call for justice as talks make limited progress

alsoReported.title: Türkiye eyes ambitious climate outcome as COP31 enters final week

article: COP31, the yearly UN climate conference, opened in Antalya, Turkey, on Nov 9 and ends Nov 20.[^13] Climate Home News describes the first week as making "limited progress".[^12] Negotiators have not yet agreed whether to produce a "cover decision", a headline political text, and some large developing countries resisted both that and any targets for particular sectors all week.[^12]

The host's flagship idea is a voluntary pledge to raise electricity's share of the world's final energy use to 35% by 2035; Climate Home puts today's share at 23%, and Hurriyet at about 20%.[^12][^13] At least 15 countries had backed it publicly.[^12] The European Union has pushed for the word "clean" electrification, which matters because electricity can still come from coal or gas, though its negotiator signalled the EU may drop the word to win more signatures.[^12][^13]

Money remains the sharpest dispute. African countries' top demand is tripling adaptation finance, money to help poorer countries cope with heat, floods and drought, to at least $120 billion a year by 2035; a draft option would only review parts of the existing finance goal.[^12] Campaign groups criticised the EU for no new finance pledges and called a proposed "just transition" mechanism weak.[^12] Brazil, last year's host, presented a voluntary roadmap that builds clean energy first and moves to phasing out coal, oil and gas after 2031.[^12]

This week ministers take over the talks. Australia's Chris Bowen, who leads the negotiations, says they cover 160 agenda items, and Turkey's COP president Murat Kurum says the hosts want an ambitious result.[^13] My read: a deal is likely to be agreed by consensus, which tends to produce cautious wording; the useful thing to watch is whether any numbers, like the 35% target or a finance figure, survive into the final text.
topics.differences: Developing countries say richer nations must pay more before they accept new targets; the EU says it is being pragmatic and has made no new finance pledge, which campaign groups criticise.[^12] Estimates of electricity's current share differ (23% vs about 20%).[^12][^13]

topics.heading: Reports say Huang weighs a return to Nvidia as its first results without him loom
topics.summary: The Financial Times reports that ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is discussing a comeback, days before Nvidia reports results on Nov 17.[^16] Anthropic plans to price its share sale on Nov 18 at a value of up to $1.45 trillion.[^14]

lead.title: Nvidia's first post-Jensen earnings and Anthropic's IPO: What to watch this week

alsoReported.title: Jensen Huang weighs Nvidia CEO comeback as ally plans 'war room': report
Nvidia earnings — along with the baggage — top next week's markets

article: This week is a test for the companies at the centre of the AI boom. Nvidia, which makes most of the chips used to train AI, reports quarterly results after markets close on Tuesday, Nov 17.[^15] It will be the first report since Jensen Huang, who co-founded the company, resigned on Nov 12 amid reports of affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy; finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO.[^15][^16]

According to the Financial Times, as reported by Fox Business, Huang is discussing with confidants whether to return, and an ally is gathering tech executives to lobby Nvidia's board and seek White House support.[^16] An online petition backing him claims more than 150,000 signatures, though the signers' identities are self-reported.[^16] Nvidia has not confirmed any of this.

Analysts expect revenue of about $109 billion, up nearly 50% from a year earlier.[^15] A Yahoo Finance editor argues the scandal will not hit sales this quarter or next because orders are placed far in advance.[^14] Investors are less sure: Nvidia shares have fallen 24% since the first New York Times report on Oct 29, and nine firms have downgraded the stock.[^15]

Meanwhile Anthropic, the AI company that makes Claude, plans to price its initial public offering (IPO, a first sale of shares to the public) on Wednesday and start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker "ANT".[^14] It is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78, which would value it at $1.3 to $1.45 trillion, and has reported $33.2 billion in revenue for the nine months to Sept. 30.[^14] Note: Anthropic makes the model that writes this brief.
My read: these two events will be read as a verdict on whether AI spending is paying off. Strong numbers would ease fears of a bubble for now; weak ones could deepen the recent sell-off.
topics.differences: Huang's allies say the tech industry wants him back; analysts who downgraded the stock see the leadership turmoil as a risk.[^16][^15] The comeback report rests on one newspaper's sources and has not been confirmed by Nvidia.[^16]

topics.heading: ASEAN leaders meet in Manila, with energy shortages and US tariffs on the agenda
topics.summary: Southeast Asian leaders opened their summit in Manila, with fuel shortages from the Iran war, US tariffs and the South China Sea on the agenda.[^17] Trump joins on Nov 17 before flying to China for APEC.[^17][^18]

lead.title: ASEAN summit: Who's attending and what's at stake?

alsoReported.title: Trump is headed to China this week. Jensen Huang won't be on the trip, but Elon Musk will.

article: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), a bloc of 11 countries with nearly 694 million people, opened its summit in Manila, the Philippine capital, on Nov 15; it runs to Nov 17.[^17] Guests include India's Narendra Modi, Brazil's Lula da Silva, Russia's foreign minister Sergey Lavrov and Canada's Mark Carney.[^17]

Energy is the most pressing issue. The war involving Iran has disrupted oil and gas supplies from the Gulf, and the Philippines declared a national energy emergency in March.[^17] Trade is next: ASEAN countries have faced US tariff increases of 10 to 12.5% since Trump's second term began.[^17] Trump holds a special US-ASEAN summit on Nov 17 and is expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand before flying to APEC in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19.[^17][^18]

Older disputes are still open. A code of conduct for the South China Sea, where China's claims overlap with those of several ASEAN members, has been under negotiation since 2005.[^17] Al Jazeera also notes border clashes between Thailand and Cambodia that killed at least 150 people and displaced nearly a million, and smoke from Indonesian wildfires linked to at least 3,500 deaths.[^17]

Why it matters: Southeast Asia sits between the US and China and trades heavily with both. One analyst described Trump's APEC visit as "essentially being a courtesy call", suggesting low expectations for big deals.[^18] My read: this week's two summits will show whether countries in the region can win tariff relief from Washington without damaging ties with Beijing.

topics.heading: A rights group says a Sudanese army drone strike killed 15 in West Kordofan
topics.summary: A Sudanese monitoring group says an army drone strike on Abu Qalb in West Kordofan killed 15 people on Sunday, including four children.[^19] The army had not commented in the report.

lead.title: Sudan army strike kills 15, including children: rights group, survivor

article: Sudan's civil war, fought since April 2023 between the national army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), is now centred on the Kordofan region in the middle of the country. On Sunday, Nov 15, a drone strike hit Abu Qalb in West Kordofan.[^19]

The Kordofan Observatory, a local monitoring group, says the army carried out the strike, that 15 people were killed, including four children who were playing football, and that it injured others and burned homes.[^19] AFP describes it as a "double-tap" strike, meaning a second hit on the same place shortly after the first.[^19] A survivor told AFP that nine of the dead were his relatives.[^19] The report does not include a response from the army, and the figures have not been independently confirmed.

My read: Kordofan has become a main front of the war, and both sides use drones near towns where civilians live. This report comes from a single news agency quoting a local group, so treat the details as provisional until others confirm them.
